title: What the Meal Leaves Behind
logline: A family cooks for two days to welcome someone home, and afterwards, over the same plates and the same effort, one of them feels only relief, another quiet pride, and another something older that they did not expect.
human_question: Can the very same act of care mean completely different things to the people who remember it?

situation.what_happens: A household prepares for a large family occasion that they themselves have chosen to make: days of cooking, borrowed pots, neighbours drawn in, money spent that is not easily spared. The occasion happens once and is shared by everyone in the house. Afterwards, separately and in their own time, the people who made it describe it differently: one remembers the relief, one the expense, one their own part in it with satisfaction, one something unresolved that the occasion brought back. Nothing about the event changed; what changed is who is remembering it.
situation.who_is_involved: The members of a household who did the work, who are usually not the ones the occasion is for; the person the occasion is about; the neighbours and relatives who lent pots, hands or money and now have a claim on the memory too.
situation.what_is_at_stake: Money and days of work, and something harder: whether the effort is seen. A shared occasion can settle an old grievance or sharpen it, and the people who did most of the cooking are often the ones least asked about it afterwards.
situation.how_it_unfolds: Occasions like this build to a single day and then release slowly. The interesting part is the aftermath, when people go back to ordinary work and the event begins to be told. Whether anyone says anything honest about it, and to whom, is entirely theirs to decide.

concept_merge.why_together: C082's object condition is worked out in the sources at length with almost this example: the memory of one's own act of giving can support quiet gladness, or pride, or possessiveness ('my good deed'), or doubt, or regret — the act stays the same and the state of mind that takes it up decides what comes of it. C075 supplies nutriment in its bounded sense: edible food is one of the four nutriments, and what the term names is support by something that has to keep arriving, not nourishment as a warm idea. A real family occasion is the one situation in ordinary life where a single, shared, indisputable event is later taken up by several people at once.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: Together they show that a person's history is not fixed in its effects: it keeps being picked up as raw material by whatever state of mind reaches for it now. What becomes visible is the source's blunt point that even generosity, remembered with self-satisfaction, can feed conceit — without anyone in the film being judged for it.

concept_links.why: The object condition is illustrated at length in the Pradeepika by the memory of one's own giving supporting gladness, pride, possessiveness, doubt or regret; the object does not settle what arises, the mind that takes it up does.

Edible food is one of the four nutriments the sources name, and nutriment means support by something that has to keep arriving rather than support by a single push. The film may use only that bounded sense: the other three nutriments are contact, intention and consciousness, the sources call all four nutriments because they keep the round of rebirth going, and nothing here may slide into a warm claim about feeding a household or feeding a mind.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: One shared event can become several different things depending on who takes it up afterwards, and even a generous act, remembered a certain way, can feed pride rather than gladness.
what_must_be_real: The family's actual relationships and history. Nothing private may be prompted, and nobody may be interviewed toward a revelation; what is said is what they choose to say.
position_hint: middle: it would sit among the group's films about kinds of support rather than about sequence, because its condition is an object taken up rather than a chain followed.
risks: Pushing family members toward a revealing interview.
Turning private feeling into an illustration of a doctrine.
Filming a tension that the family has not agreed, specifically and afterwards, to have shown.

Letting nutriment become a wellness idea about feeding people well or feeding the mind good things; the sources call these nutriments because they keep the round of rebirth going, and their aim is its ending.
drop_if: No family is willing to speak honestly, separately, about mixed feelings.
No comparable real occasion falls within the filming window.

connections.note: The fish chain ends at a table; this idea begins there and asks what the meal becomes in memory.
Both look at what a long shared effort leaves behind once it is over.

selection.reason: Held: strong and well grounded in the object-condition passages, but the group's eight slots are filled and C082 is already carried by three kept ideas; hold it for the object condition, which no film on the current slate shows.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
